---
title: "memdash handoff workflow: vibe code ↔ RStudio Server ↔ on-site GitLab"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, comment = "#")
```

> This sandbox ("vibe code") **cannot reach the on-site GitLab** (firewalled).
> All exchange happens as **`git bundle` / `git format-patch` files** moved
> through an approved channel (file transfer, USB, ...).
> **GitLab `main` is the source of truth.** The GitHub PR is a frozen mirror.
>
> Convention: vibe works on `vibe/<slug>-d02277` branches here; you merge to
> `main` on GitLab. Bundles = full history sync; patches = small reviewable diffs.

## 0. One-time setup in RStudio Server

Run this **bash** chunk in the RStudio **Terminal** tab:

```{bash}
cd ~/projects                                   # wherever you keep projects
# First time: clone from the bundle file vibe gave you
# git clone /path/to/memdash-outgoing.bundle memdash
cd memdash
# Attach the on-site GitLab repo (SSH key or HTTPS + token configured once)
git remote add gitlab https://gitlab.corp.example/<group>/memdash.git
git push -u gitlab --all && git push -u gitlab --tags
```

Optional but recommended — pin R package versions on this machine:

```{r}
setwd("~/projects/memdash/r-package/memdash")
renv::init()        # creates renv/ + renv.lock
renv::snapshot()
```

## 1. vibe → you: take a new bundle / patch set

Vibe produces one of these (you just transfer the file):

```{bash}
# in the vibe sandbox:
git bundle create ~/memdash-outgoing.bundle vibe/memdash-shiny-d02277
# or, for a small change:
git format-patch main..vibe/memdash-shiny-d02277 -o ~/memdash-patches/
```

**In RStudio Terminal**, apply it:

```{bash}
cd ~/projects/memdash
# bundle:
git fetch /path/to/memdash-outgoing.bundle 'refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/incoming/*'
git checkout -B work main
# git merge incoming/vibe/memdash-shiny-d02277
# patch series instead:
# git am /path/to/memdash-patches/*.patch
git push gitlab work:main
```

## 2. Test the R package in RStudio (R chunk)

```{r}
setwd("~/projects/memdash/r-package/memdash")
reticulate::py_install("neo4j")   # once per Python env
devtools::load_all()              # load without installing
testthat::test_local()            # tests/ — no live Memgraph needed
devtools::check()                 # full R CMD check
# click-through against your Memgraph (tenant db defaults to stxp4rd):
memdash::run_memdash()
# programmatic smoke test:
memdash::memgraph_connect("bolt://<memgraph-host>:7687", database = "stxp4rd")
memdash::memdash_seed_demo()
res <- memdash::memgraph_query("MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes")
memdash::records_to_df(res$records, res$fields)
memdash::memgraph_disconnect()
```

If you fix something locally:

```{bash}
cd ~/projects/memdash
git add -A && git commit -m "fix: <what>" && git push gitlab HEAD:main
```

## 3. You → vibe: send your tested state back

```{bash}
cd ~/projects/memdash
git bundle create /path/to/memdash-incoming.bundle main     # full history
# or: git format-patch origin/main..HEAD -o /path/to/patches/
```

Transfer the file back. Vibe then runs, in the sandbox:

```{bash}
cd /workspace/github__JannikVindeloev__memdash
git fetch /path/to/memdash-incoming.bundle 'refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/yours/*'
git checkout -b vibe/continue-d02277 yours/main
# patches instead: git am /path/to/patches/*.patch
```

…develops on `vibe/continue-d02277`, and produces the next `memdash-outgoing.bundle`. Loop closed.

## 4. House rules

1. Never hand-edit bundle files; regenerate them with `git bundle create`.
2. GitLab credentials live only in your credential helper / SSH — never commit tokens.
3. Add `.Renviron` to the root `.gitignore`; R artifacts are already covered by `r-package/memdash/.gitignore`.
4. Web app (`src/`) travels in the same bundles — run `npm install` on whichever side needs it (`node_modules` is gitignored).
5. If both sides touched the same file, resolve on your side in RStudio and send back a bundle.
